claims.text: US President Donald Trump declared a breakthrough in negotiations over the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza and the withdrawal of Israeli forces.
Far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir dismissed the proposed Gaza deal as 'unacceptable'.
Hamas negotiator Ghazi Hamad stated Hamas will hand over its weapons to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza on condition of an Israeli troop withdrawal.
US President Donald Trump stated the US would be hitting Iran 'very hard' in the coming weeks.
The preliminary Gaza deal framework was reached following a meeting of mediators from Egypt, Qatar, Turkiye, and the United States.
At least 73,341 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza during the conflict.
At least 1,214 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the October ceasefire agreement took effect.
Medical authorities in Gaza reported one Palestinian killed and several wounded in Israeli airstrikes and gunfire shortly after Trump's announcement.

Under the 15-point roadmap published by the Board of Peace, the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza will oversee the decommissioning and storage of heavy weapons, production sites, and tunnels.
An annex to the proposed plan requires Israeli forces to withdraw to the Yellow Line within 24 hours of approval by the Israeli government.
Spanish authorities reported that at least 57 people died trying to reach the enclave of Ceuta from Morocco.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described the entry of tens of thousands of migrants into Ceuta as a violation of Spain's territorial integrity.
Spain's interior ministry stated that over 48,300 migrants had voluntarily returned to Morocco by 6pm on Friday.
Spain's Supreme Court recently ruled that migrants intercepted at sea entering Ceuta or Melilla cannot be summarily returned without processing.
US President Donald Trump told Fox News that the border crossing in Ceuta demonstrates what will happen in the US in three years if Democrats win.
South American football governing body CONMEBOL requested further information from FIFA regarding its plan to sell private stakes in its tournament business.
Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, resigned in protest against FIFA's private investment plan.
European football governing body UEFA voted to boycott World Cups if FIFA proceeds with selling stakes to private investors.
FIFA proposed creating a commercial subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise, in which private investors could buy minority stakes.
FIFA Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour stated that FIFA staff were deceived by Gianni Infantino regarding the World Cup sell-off proposal.
An avalanche struck a 10-person climbing expedition led by Nirmal Purja on Pakistan's Broad Peak.
Rescuers recovered the remains of 39-year-old American climber Mallory Geis from San Antonio, Texas.
The bodies of Omani climber Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy and Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung were identified following the avalanche.
GPS tracking data indicated the avalanche occurred at 6,579 metres elevation on the west ridge of Broad Peak.
Nirmal Purja set a world record in 2019 by climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre-plus peaks in just over six months.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a video message stating he forgives young protesters who hurled abuses at him and his late mother.
Congress leader Pawan Khera criticized PM Modi's video message, saying the country asked Modi to apologize but Modi instead forgave the country.
Youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests against NEET medical exam paper leaks led to the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
A Zero FIR registered in Noida over abusive remarks against PM Modi during the Jantar Mantar protest was transferred to Delhi Police on July 31.
Suspected terrorists shot two non-local brick kiln workers in Kellam, Kulgam district, killing one and injuring another.
Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha strongly condemned the attack and instructed security forces to eliminate the perpetrators.
The deceased worker in the Kulgam attack was identified as 24-year-old Deepak Ratray, while the injured worker was identified as 28-year-old Bopinder, both from Chhattisgarh.
A Delhi court sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the 2020 murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma.
Additional Sessions Judge Parveen Kumar Singh rejected the prosecution's plea for the death penalty, ruling the state failed to prove specific individual acts during the murder.
Tahir Hussain joined AIMIM in December 2024 and finished third in the 2025 Delhi Assembly election in Mustafabad.
Following his sentencing, Tahir Hussain stated to reporters that he would get justice from the High Court.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham held their first telephone conversation on July 31, 2026.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham appointed Indian-born Kanishka Narayan as a cabinet minister heading AI policy.
The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) was operationalised on July 15, 2026.
Modi and Burnham agreed to work closely together towards de-escalation of the West Asia crisis and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
The India Meteorological Department forecast below-normal average rainfall in India for the August-September period due to El Niño risks.
IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra stated 24 days in July were under the influence of low pressure systems compared to the normal 13.5 days.
UN Secretary General António Guterres stated that a strengthening El Niño is 'adding fuel to a planet already on fire' and pushing climate conditions into uncharted territory.
The Bhakra Beas Management Board increased total water discharge from Pandoh Dam into the Beas River to nearly 36,000 cusecs.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar spoke with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, urging an end to attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers.
Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh informed Parliament that 2,557 Indian nationals have been evacuated from Iran via Armenia or Azerbaijan.
An Indian sailor was killed and six others injured when two Emirati oil tankers were struck by Iranian missiles in the Strait of Hormuz earlier in July.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for drone and missile attacks on US-operated military facilities in Kuwait.
